sections.title: Please and you're welcome
sections.content: *Légy szíves* means "please" (literally "be so kind") — tack it onto a request to make it politer, or use it alone to accept something offered. In everyday speech it's often shortened to *légyszi*. *Szívesen* is the standard reply to *köszönöm* ("thank you"), matching English "you're welcome".

*Légy szíves* also works standing completely alone as an answer: offered something and you want it, *légy szíves* (or the casual *légyszi*) on its own means "please, yes." You may also hear *kérlek* for "please" — it's less common and leans more toward "I'm asking you" than a simple politeness word.
